WORK.title: Mark
WORK.subtitle: This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God
intro: Mark is the shortest and fastest-moving of the four Gospels. It opens with John the Baptist crying out in the wilderness and, with almost no preamble, brings the reader to Jesus' side: calling disciples, healing the sick, driving out unclean spirits, calming the storm...

Mark keeps the story moving with words like "immediately" and "at once", like a documentary whose camera never stops. The whole book keeps asking one question: "Who is this man?" Until the centurion at the foot of the cross says: "Truly this man was the Son of God!"
Each chapter is adapted from Mark in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

matthew.title: Matthew
matthew.subtitle: The King of the kingdom of heaven
intro: Matthew is the first book of the New Testament. It opens with a family tree: a descendant of Abraham, a son of David, counted generation by generation down to Jesus, telling the reader that the promises of the Old Testament are fulfilled here.

Matthew writes for readers who know the Old Testament well and often says, "This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet." Five long discourses (the Sermon on the Mount, the sending of the Twelve, the parables of the kingdom, life among the disciples, and the teaching on the Mount of Olives) portray Jesus as the King and Teacher of the kingdom of heaven. The book opens with "Immanuel" and closes with "surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age."
Each chapter is adapted from Matthew in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

luke.title: Luke
luke.subtitle: The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost
intro: Luke is the third book of the New Testament. Its author, Luke, was a physician who says he "carefully investigated everything from the beginning" and wrote an orderly account for Theophilus: it begins at the altar of incense in the temple with the old priest Zechariah, and ends with the disciples praising God in the temple.

Luke pays special attention to people others overlooked: shepherds, widows, tax collectors, Samaritans, a prodigal son and a criminal. Many stories are recorded only by Luke: the shepherds at the manger, the Good Samaritan, the lost sheep, the lost coin and the prodigal son, Zacchaeus, the criminal who repented on the cross, and the road to Emmaus. The thread running through the book is "the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost."
Each chapter is adapted from Luke in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

john.title: John
john.subtitle: The Word became flesh
intro: John is the fourth book of the New Testament. Its author is John, the disciple whom Jesus loved. He begins with "In the beginning was the Word" and records seven signs and the words Jesus spoke of Himself: "I am the bread of life," "I am the light of the world," "I am the good shepherd," "I am the resurrection and the life."

John records much that the other three Gospels do not: water turned into wine at the wedding in Cana, Nicodemus coming to Jesus at night, the Samaritan woman at the well, Lazarus walking out of the tomb, the night Jesus washed the disciples' feet in the upper room, and "Mary" spoken in the garden at dawn. The thread running through the whole book is life and light: "these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name."
Each chapter is adapted from John in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

acts.title: Acts
acts.subtitle: The gospel to the ends of the earth
intro: Acts is the fifth book of the New Testament and the sequel to the Gospel of Luke. Its author, Luke, begins with Jesus' ascension and records the Holy Spirit coming at Pentecost, as the disciples set out from Jerusalem to be His witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.

The first half follows Peter: the lame man at the Beautiful Gate leaping up to walk, Stephen's martyrdom, Philip baptizing the Ethiopian official on the desert road, and Cornelius's household receiving the Holy Spirit. The second half follows Paul, the persecutor who became an apostle: three missionary journeys, songs at midnight in the Philippian jail, his address on the Areopagus in Athens, fourteen days of storm at sea, and at last Rome, where he boldly proclaimed the kingdom of God.
Each chapter is adapted from Acts in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

romans.title: Romans
romans.subtitle: Justified by faith
intro: Romans is Paul's letter to the believers in Rome. He had not yet been to Rome. Wintering in Corinth at the home of Gaius, he dictated it to Tertius, who wrote it down, and Phoebe, a servant of the church at Cenchrea, carried it across the sea.

This comic sets the whole letter in two places. By an evening lamp in Corinth, Paul paces as he speaks it line by line; in the workshop at the home of Priscilla and Aquila in Rome, a room of Jews and Gentiles hears it read aloud before dawn. They bow their heads at “all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,” and look up at “justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.” As the reading reaches “The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near,” the first light of morning slips in through the door.
Each chapter is adapted from Romans in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

chapters.1: The Power of God for Salvation

corinthians1.title: 1 Corinthians
corinthians1.subtitle: Love is patient
intro: 1 Corinthians is Paul's letter from Ephesus to the church in Corinth. Some from Chloe's household had reported “there are quarrels among you,” and the Corinthians themselves had written with questions, so Paul answers them one by one: factions, lawsuits, marriage, food sacrificed to idols, the Lord's Supper, spiritual gifts, and the resurrection.

This comic sets the whole letter in two places. In the workshop of Aquila and Priscilla in Ephesus, Paul dictates over several early mornings while Sosthenes writes it down; in the courtyard of Gaius's house in Corinth, a roomful of divided people listens from afternoon deep into the night. When the reading reaches “the greatest of these is love,” the whole room lifts their faces; at “Where, O Death, is your victory?” golden light falls a second time under a sky full of stars.
Each chapter is adapted from 1 Corinthians in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

chapters.8: Do Not Make a Brother Stumble

corinthians2.title: 2 Corinthians
corinthians2.subtitle: Power made perfect in weakness
intro: 2 Corinthians is Paul's second letter to the church in Corinth, written from Macedonia. At Troas he could not find Titus, so he crossed the sea to Macedonia, where there were “conflicts on the outside, fears within,” until Titus came back from Corinth with news of the Corinthians' longing and zeal. The letter holds comfort and reconciliation, the collection for the saints in Jerusalem, and a heavy-hearted answer to those who looked down on him.

This comic sets the whole letter in two places. In the upper room of Lydia's house in Philippi, Paul dictates from a grey late-autumn day, to the first warm light when Titus arrives, to a single lamp on another evening, while Timothy writes it down. In the courtyard of Gaius's house in Corinth, Titus reads from early morning until noon; when he reaches “My grace is sufficient for you,” golden light falls on a tearful face lifted up beneath the lamp.
Each chapter is adapted from 2 Corinthians in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

chapters.6: Now Is the Time of Favor
chapters.8: He Became Poor for Your Sake

galatians.title: Galatians
galatians.subtitle: Freedom in Christ
intro: Galatians is Paul's urgent letter to the churches of Galatia. Visitors had come telling the disciples around Lystra that believing in Christ was not enough—they must also be circumcised and keep the law—and the believers were wavering. Paul begins with “I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel”: no thanksgiving, no long greetings. At the end he takes the pen himself and finishes in large letters with his own hand.

This comic sets the whole letter in two places. In a large house of the church in Antioch of Syria, Paul dictates under the hard white light of late summer while Titus writes it down; when he reaches “I no longer live, but Christ lives in me,” the light turns gold. In a dirt courtyard by the gate of Lystra, an elder reads from a windy, overcast afternoon until dusk. People who once watched Paul being stoned sit listening there, and the child of a slave runs into the father's arms, crying “Abba.”
Each chapter is adapted from Galatians in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

ephesians.title: Ephesians
ephesians.subtitle: The Body of Christ
intro: Ephesians is the letter Paul wrote as a prisoner in Rome, a chain linking him to the soldier who guarded him. There is nothing in it to rebuke: the first three chapters are one long song of praise and prayer—the dead are made alive, and the wall between the Gentiles and Israel is torn down; the last three are about living together—unity, putting off the old self, husbands and wives, parents and children, masters and slaves at home, and finally “the full armor of God.”

This comic sets the whole letter in two places. In a rented house in Rome, Paul dictates from early morning until dusk while Tychicus writes it down; when he reaches “it is by grace you have been saved through faith,” the light from the high window turns gold. In the lecture hall of Tyrannus in Ephesus, the elders read from noon until sunset. Those who once burned their books sit by the door holding empty chests, and Trophimus—the man on whose account Paul was seized—sits alone at the very edge.
Each chapter is adapted from Ephesians in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

chapters.3: Wide and Long and High and Deep

philippians.title: Philippians
philippians.subtitle: Rejoice in the Lord Always
intro: Philippians is the letter Paul wrote in chains in Rome to the first church he had planted in Europe. He did not yet know whether he would live or die, yet the letter is full of joy: “For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.” At its center is the hymn of Christ who emptied Himself—though He existed in the form of God, He took the form of a servant and became obedient to death. It ends with “Rejoice in the Lord always,” and “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.”

This comic sets the whole letter in two places. In a rented house in Rome, Paul dictates in chains while Timothy writes it down, and Epaphroditus, only just recovered from his illness, sits in the corner. In the courtyard of Lydia’s house in Philippi, the former jailer stands under the colonnade and reads the letter aloud; when he reaches “every knee should bow,” the whole courtyard kneels in golden light. Euodia and Syntyche, two sisters who could not agree, begin at opposite ends of the courtyard, and both look up at the same moment when their names are read.
Each chapter is adapted from Philippians in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

colossians.title: Colossians
colossians.subtitle: Christ, Supreme over All
intro: Colossians is the letter Paul wrote in chains in Rome to a church he had never visited. The gospel had been carried home to the Lycus Valley by Epaphras, one of their own, and now some there were teaching “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!” Paul does not scold. The whole letter speaks of how great one Person is: “in Him all things were created,” and “He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.” So they are to be rooted and built up in Him, to put off the old self and put on the new, and “whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord.”

This comic sets the whole letter in two places. In a rented house in Rome, Paul dictates in chains while Timothy writes it down; Epaphras sits across from them, and later kneels in the corner, wrestling in prayer for them. In the courtyard of a house in Colossae, Tychicus reads the letter from morning until the lamps are lit, with Onesimus, a man of that city, standing half a step behind him. When he reaches “in Him all things hold together,” golden light spills down from the snowy peaks and the whole courtyard lifts its face.
Each chapter is adapted from Colossians in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

chapters.1: In Him All Things Hold Together
chapters.3: Set Your Minds on Things Above

thessalonians1.title: 1 Thessalonians
thessalonians1.subtitle: The Hope of the Lord's Return
intro: 1 Thessalonians is Paul's earliest letter. He had preached in Thessalonica for only three Sabbaths before the brothers sent him out of the city by night; by the time he reached Corinth, Timothy came back with the news: the believers there had not scattered. The letter holds no rebuke, only longing: “like a nursing mother caring for her children.” It also answers the thing that hurt them most. Some among them had fallen asleep, and those still living were grieving “like the rest, who are without hope.” Paul tells them that when the Lord comes, “we will always be with the Lord.” It closes with a string of short charges: “Rejoice at all times. Pray without ceasing. Give thanks in every circumstance.”

This comic sets the whole letter in two places. In Aquila's workshop in Corinth, Paul dictates with a tentmaker's needle still in his hand, Silas writes it down, and Timothy, just back from the road, sits beside them. In Jason's house in Thessalonica, behind a door once kicked in and now nailed with fresh boards, the letter is read by lamplight before dawn. Among the listeners are a potter who carried the little clay idols out of his house, and a widow who has just buried her husband, holding a small boy by the hand. When the reading reaches the Lord's coming, the sun rises out of the sea, golden light floods the room, and every face lifts.

Each chapter is adapted from 1 Thessalonians in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

thessalonians2.title: 2 Thessalonians
thessalonians2.subtitle: Stand Firm in What You Were Taught
intro: 2 Thessalonians was written from Corinth by Paul, Silas, and Timothy not long after the first letter was sent. The persecution had not stopped, yet the letter opens by saying “your faith is growing more and more.” A letter was going around the city under Paul's name, claiming that the Day of the Lord had already come, and some were so shaken they had stopped working. Paul writes that they are “not to be easily disconcerted or alarmed,” and tells them to “stand firm.” To those who used waiting for the Lord as an excuse to sit idle and eat other people's bread, he speaks plainly: “If anyone is unwilling to work, he shall not eat.” And he adds: “Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.”

This comic picks up from 1 Thessalonians in the same two places. In the workshop in Corinth, Paul dictates late at night with a needle between his fingers. In Jason's house in Thessalonica, one more fresh board has been nailed across the door, and at dusk people come in from work to hear the letter. When the reading reaches the Lord revealed from heaven in blazing fire, the sunset at the doorway lights up the lifted faces of the widow and the little boy. At the end, the potter puts a lump of wet clay into the idle man's hands, and that night guides his hands at the wheel as he learns to work it.

Each chapter is adapted from 2 Thessalonians in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

chapters.3: Do Not Grow Weary in Doing Good

timothy1.title: 1 Timothy
timothy1.subtitle: Order in the Church
intro: 1 Timothy is the letter Paul wrote after leaving for Macedonia, to Timothy, who had stayed behind in Ephesus. The Saul who once dragged people off to prison now writes to teach a young man how to keep a church: “This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.” The letter covers how to pray, how to choose overseers and deacons, and how to care for widows, because the church is “the pillar and foundation of the truth.” And to his young co-worker he says: “Let no one despise your youth,” and “Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life.”

This comic is set in two places. In the courtyard of Lydia's house in Philippi, where purple linen hangs drying, Paul writes the letter line by line in his own hand. In the lecture hall of Tyrannus in Ephesus, Timothy grips the scroll and reads from the very edge of the stone steps while someone in the front row snickers. From early morning to dusk, chapter by chapter, he makes his way to the middle of the steps, and a white-haired elder is the first to nod. The widow under the farthest pillar is taken home, and the last of the sunset fills the courtyard. At the end, in a small room at night, Timothy lays the letter in a wooden box and rests his hand on it.
Each chapter is adapted from 1 Timothy in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

chapters.5: Honor Widows Who Are Truly in Need

timothy2.title: 2 Timothy
timothy2.subtitle: The Good Fight
intro: 2 Timothy is Paul's last letter. He is a prisoner in Rome for the second time: “For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand.” Winter is coming, and the people around him have scattered; “Only Luke is with me.” He writes “to Timothy, my beloved child”: “For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.” Though he himself is in chains, he says, “But the word of God cannot be chained!” He tells Timothy to hold on to the Scriptures he has known since childhood and to preach the word, and then: “Make every effort to come to me quickly.”

This comic is set in two places. In a small stone-walled room in Rome, Paul's chain is fastened to a ring in the wall and Luke writes for him; with each chapter the room grows colder and emptier. In a small room in Ephesus at night, Timothy reads the letter alone by lamplight. On the last night, a beam of golden light comes through the high window and falls on Paul's face: “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.” At the end, Timothy boards a ship with Mark, and the weather has already turned cold.
Each chapter is adapted from 2 Timothy in comic form. The English edition quotes Scripture word for word from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB); added dialogue and narration are marked separately.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.title: The Son of God
jesus.quote: The time is fulfilled … and the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!
jesus.bio: From its first line, Mark announces that Jesus is "the Son of God." He came from Nazareth in Galilee, was baptized in the Jordan, and at once began to preach, call disciples, heal the sick and drive out unclean spirits. His authority amazed people; His compassion drew them near.

john.name: John the Baptist
john.title: Preparing the way of the Lord in the wilderness
john.quote: After me will come One more powerful than I
john.bio: A prophet clothed in camel's hair who ate locusts and wild honey. By the Jordan River he preached a baptism of repentance, prepared the way for Jesus, and baptized Jesus himself.

peter.name: Simon Peter
peter.title: A fisherman by the Sea of Galilee
peter.bio: One of the first disciples Jesus called by the sea. He left his nets at once to follow Jesus, who later gave him the name Peter. His home was in Capernaum, where Jesus healed his mother-in-law of a fever.

andrew.name: Andrew
andrew.title: Simon's brother
andrew.quote: Come, follow Me … and I will make you fishers of men.
andrew.bio: Jesus called him while he and his brother Simon were casting a net into the sea. The two brothers left their nets at once and followed Jesus.

james.name: James and John
james.title: Sons of Zebedee
james.quote: Immediately Jesus called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Him.
james.bio: Two brothers mending their nets in a boat. When Jesus called them, they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Him.

levi.name: Levi
levi.title: The man at the tax booth
levi.bio: The son of Alphaeus, a tax collector whom others looked down on. Jesus said to him, "Follow Me," and he got up and followed. Then he held a dinner at his house for many tax collectors and sinners.

leper.name: A Man with Leprosy
leper.title: He knelt and begged
leper.quote: If You are willing, You can make me clean.
leper.bio: A sick man shut out from society. He knelt before Jesus and begged Him; moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched him.

paralytic.name: The Paralytic
paralytic.title: Lowered through the roof
paralytic.bio: Four friends carried him, but the crowd kept them from getting in, so they opened up the roof and lowered him down. Seeing their faith, Jesus first forgave his sins, then told him to get up and walk.

mary.name: Mary
mary.title: The mother of Jesus
mary.quote: Whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.
mary.bio: The mother of Jesus. While Jesus was teaching in a house, she and His brothers stood outside and sent word to call Him. Later, in His hometown, people said, "Isn't this the carpenter, the son of Mary?" and took offense at Him.

demoniac.name: The Gerasene Demoniac
demoniac.title: The man from the tombs
demoniac.quote: Tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.
demoniac.bio: He lived among the tombs; no chain could hold him, and night and day he cried out and cut himself with stones. Jesus drove out the unclean spirits, and they went into the pigs. The man sat there dressed and in his right mind, then went to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him.

jairus.name: Jairus
jairus.title: A synagogue leader
jairus.quote: Do not be afraid; just believe.
jairus.bio: His little daughter was dying. He fell at Jesus' feet and pleaded with Him to come and lay His hands on her. On the way came word that she had died, but Jesus told him, "Do not be afraid; just believe," went in, took the girl by the hand and told her to get up.

bleeding_woman.name: The Woman Healed of Bleeding
bleeding_woman.title: She touched Jesus' cloak
bleeding_woman.quote: If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.
bleeding_woman.bio: She had suffered from bleeding for twelve years and endured much under many doctors, spending all she had, yet only grew worse. Pressing through the crowd, she touched Jesus' cloak from behind, and at once her bleeding stopped. Jesus said to her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you."

herod.name: King Herod
herod.title: The king who beheaded John the Baptist
herod.quote: John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead!
herod.bio: He knew John was a righteous and holy man, feared him and liked to listen to him. Yet because John told him it was not lawful to marry his brother Philip's wife Herodias, he had John bound in prison. At his birthday banquet, because of his oaths and his guests, he sent an executioner to behead John.

syrophoenician.name: The Syrophoenician Woman
syrophoenician.title: A mother pleading for her daughter
syrophoenician.quote: Yes, Lord … even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs.
syrophoenician.bio: A Greek woman in the region of Tyre whose little daughter had an unclean spirit. She fell at Jesus' feet and begged Him to drive the demon out. Jesus said, "Because of this answer, you may go"; she went home and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone.

rich_man.name: The Rich Young Man
rich_man.title: He asked about eternal life
rich_man.quote: Good Teacher … what must I do to inherit eternal life?
rich_man.bio: He ran up, knelt before Jesus and asked about eternal life, saying he had kept the commandments since his youth. Jesus looked at him and loved him, and told him to sell everything, give to the poor, and come follow Him. The man's face fell, and he went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.

bartimaeus.name: Bartimaeus
bartimaeus.title: The blind man by the road at Jericho
bartimaeus.quote: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!
bartimaeus.bio: The son of Timaeus, a blind beggar sitting beside the road. When he heard it was Jesus of Nazareth, he cried out, and all the louder when the crowd rebuked him. When Jesus called him, he threw off his cloak and jumped up. Jesus said, "Your faith has healed you," and at once he could see and followed Jesus along the road.

widow.name: The Poor Widow
widow.title: She gave two small coins
widow.quote: This poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.
widow.bio: Many rich people put large amounts into the temple treasury, but she put in only two small copper coins. Jesus said she had given more than all the others: they gave out of their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, put in all she had to live on.

judas.name: Judas Iscariot
judas.title: The disciple who betrayed Jesus
judas.quote: The One I kiss is the man
judas.bio: One of the Twelve. He went to the chief priests to hand Jesus over to them, and they promised to give him money. In Gethsemane he came with a crowd armed with swords and clubs, went straight to Jesus, said "Rabbi!" and kissed Him.

pilate.name: Pilate
pilate.title: The man who questioned Jesus
pilate.quote: Are You the King of the Jews?
pilate.bio: The chief priests bound Jesus and handed Him over to him. He knew they had handed Jesus over out of envy, yet, wishing to satisfy the crowd, he released Barabbas, had Jesus flogged and handed Him over to be crucified. Later, when Joseph of Arimathea asked for the body of Jesus, he granted it.

simon_cyrene.name: Simon of Cyrene
simon_cyrene.title: He carried the cross of Jesus
simon_cyrene.quote: The soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
simon_cyrene.bio: The father of Alexander and Rufus. He was passing by on his way in from the country when he was forced to go along and carry the cross of Jesus to Golgotha.

mary_magdalene.name: Mary Magdalene
mary_magdalene.title: The first witness of the resurrection
mary_magdalene.quote: After Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene
mary_magdalene.bio: Jesus had driven seven demons out of her. When Jesus was crucified, she and other women watched from a distance, and she saw where He was laid. When the Sabbath was over, she went to the tomb early with spices and found the stone already rolled away; the risen Jesus appeared first to her.

joseph_arimathea.name: Joseph of Arimathea
joseph_arimathea.title: A prominent Council member
joseph_arimathea.quote: A prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God
joseph_arimathea.bio: It was the day of Preparation. He boldly went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. He bought a linen cloth, took Jesus down, wrapped Him, placed Him in a tomb cut out of the rock, and rolled a stone against the entrance.

matthew.name: Matthew
matthew.title: The tax collector who became an apostle
matthew.bio: A tax collector at his booth by the town gate, whom people went out of their way to avoid. Jesus saw him and said, "Follow Me," and he got up and followed Him. Later Jesus dined at his house with many tax collectors and sinners. He was one of the Twelve, listed as "Matthew the tax collector"; Mark calls him Levi.

magi.name: The Magi
magi.title: They followed the star to worship Him
magi.quote: Where is the One who has been born King of the Jews?
magi.bio: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, Magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem, looking for the One born King of the Jews. The star they had seen went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the Child was. They entered the house, fell down and worshiped Him, and offered gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh. Warned in a dream, they returned to their country by another route.

joseph.name: Joseph
joseph.title: Husband of Mary
joseph.quote: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife
joseph.bio: The husband of Mary, a righteous man. When he learned she was with child, he did not want to disgrace her publicly and planned to divorce her quietly. An angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream; he woke, took Mary as his wife as he was told, and named the Child Jesus. Warned again in a dream, he fled with the Child and His mother to Egypt, and after Herod died he settled in Nazareth.

centurion.name: The Centurion
centurion.title: An officer who pleaded for his servant
centurion.quote: just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
centurion.bio: When Jesus entered Capernaum, this officer with soldiers under him came pleading: his servant lay at home paralyzed and in terrible suffering. He said he was not worthy to have Jesus come under his roof and asked only for a word. Jesus marveled, saying He had not found such great faith in anyone in Israel, and the servant was healed at that very hour.

zacchaeus.name: Zacchaeus
zacchaeus.title: The tax collector who climbed a tree
zacchaeus.quote: Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.
zacchaeus.bio: A chief tax collector in Jericho, and very wealthy. When Jesus passed through, he could not see Him over the crowd because he was short, so he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree. Jesus looked up and told him to hurry down, for He must stay at his house today, and everyone began to grumble that Jesus had gone to be the guest of a sinner. Zacchaeus stood up and said he would give half of his possessions to the poor and repay fourfold anyone he had cheated. Jesus said, "Today salvation has come to this house."

martha.name: Martha and Mary
martha.title: The sisters who welcomed Jesus
martha.quote: Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.
martha.bio: Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home. Her sister Mary sat at the Lord's feet listening to His message, while Martha, distracted by all the preparations, asked Jesus to tell her sister to help her. The Lord replied, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things. But only one thing is necessary."

simeon.name: Simeon
simeon.title: The old man who held the Child in the temple
simeon.quote: my eyes have seen Your salvation
simeon.bio: A righteous and devout man in Jerusalem, waiting for the consolation of Israel. The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not die before he had seen the Lord's Christ. When the parents brought the Child into the temple, Simeon took Him in his arms and said, "Sovereign Lord, as You have promised, You now dismiss Your servant in peace." He also told Mary that a sword would pierce her own soul.

penitent.name: The Repentant Criminal
penitent.title: The man crucified beside Jesus
penitent.quote: Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!
penitent.bio: One of the two criminals crucified with Jesus. When the other heaped abuse on Jesus, he rebuked him: "We are punished justly... But this man has done nothing wrong." Then he said, "Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!" And Jesus said to him, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise."

nicodemus.name: Nicodemus
nicodemus.title: The leader who came to Jesus at night
nicodemus.quote: no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.
nicodemus.bio: A Pharisee and a leader of the Jews. He came to Jesus at night and called Him a teacher who has come from God. Jesus told him, "Truly, truly, I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again." "How can this be?" Nicodemus asked. Later, when the chief priests and Pharisees wanted to seize Jesus, he spoke up for Him; and after the crucifixion he brought about seventy-five pounds of myrrh and aloes and buried Jesus together with Joseph of Arimathea.

samaritan_woman.name: The Samaritan Woman
samaritan_woman.title: The woman who came to draw water
samaritan_woman.quote: Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did.
samaritan_woman.bio: A woman of Sychar who came to Jacob's well about noon to draw water. Jesus, sitting by the well, asked her for a drink and told her the water He gives becomes a fount springing up to eternal life. He told her she had had five husbands, and then said, "I who speak to you am He." She left her water jar, went back into the town, and said to the people, "Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?" Many Samaritans from that town believed because of her testimony.

lazarus.name: Lazarus
lazarus.title: The man who came out of the tomb
lazarus.bio: A man of Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, whom Jesus loved. He fell sick and died, and when Jesus arrived he had already been in the tomb four days. Jesus wept at the tomb, told them to take away the stone, and called out in a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out!" The man who had been dead came out, his hands and feet bound in strips of linen and his face wrapped in a cloth. Many of the Jews came to believe in Jesus on account of him, so the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well.

thomas.name: Thomas
thomas.title: The disciple who wanted to see for himself
thomas.bio: One of the Twelve, called Didymus. He was not with the disciples when the risen Jesus first came to them, and he said, "Unless I see the nail marks in His hands... I will never believe." Eight days later Jesus came again and said to him, "Put your finger here and look at My hands... Stop doubting and believe." Thomas replied, "My Lord and my God!" Jesus said, "Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed."

sea.desc: Parables from a boat, a storm stilled at sea, and Jairus's daughter raised

road.desc: Three times He foretells His suffering on the way to Jerusalem

m_entry.desc: Riding in on a donkey, cleansing the temple, and teaching on the Mount of Olives

l_grace.desc: Proclaimed in Nazareth: healing, forgiving, raising the dead

l_parables.desc: Told one after another on the way to Jerusalem

l_cross.desc: From the Last Supper to the cross and the tomb

l_emmaus.title: The Lord Has Really Risen
l_emmaus.desc: The empty tomb, a walk together, eyes opened at the bread

j_light.desc: The Word became flesh, John testified, the first disciples came

j_signs.title: Signs That You May Believe
j_signs.desc: From water into wine at Cana to Lazarus coming out of the tomb

j_iam.title: I Am …
j_iam.desc: Bread of life, light of the world, good shepherd, the true vine

j_upper.title: Last Words to His Own
j_upper.desc: Washing feet, love one another, peace, a prayer for them

j_cross.title: His Life for the Sheep
j_cross.desc: Arrested in the garden, tried by Pilate, finished on the cross

j_risen.title: I Have Seen the Lord
j_risen.desc: The empty tomb, the locked room, breakfast by the sea

miracles.desc: See the mighty power of God

faith.desc: Do not be afraid; just believe.

parables.title: Parables
parables.desc: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

prayer.title: Prayer
prayer.desc: While it was still dark, He slipped out to a solitary place to pray

cross.title: The Cross
cross.desc: To give His life as a ransom for many

risen.title: Risen
risen.desc: He has risen! He is not here!

forgive.title: Forgiveness and Healing
forgive.desc: The Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins

sabbath.title: The Sabbath
sabbath.desc: The Sabbath was made for man

repent.title: Repentance and the Gospel
repent.desc: The kingdom of God is near.

newold.title: New and Old
newold.desc: New wine is poured into new wineskins.

capernaum.name: Capernaum
capernaum.desc: Jesus' home base in Galilee: the unclean spirit driven out in the synagogue, Peter's mother-in-law healed, and the paralytic lowered through the roof all happened here.

sea.name: Sea of Galilee
sea.desc: By this sea Jesus called the fishermen and taught the crowds from a boat; on it He calmed the storm and walked on the water.

nazareth.name: Nazareth
nazareth.desc: Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee to be baptized in the Jordan; later He returned to His hometown, but its people took offense at Him.

jordan.name: Jordan River
jordan.desc: John baptized here. When Jesus was baptized here, the heavens broke open and the Spirit descended on Him.

wilderness.name: Wilderness
wilderness.desc: John preached in the wilderness. After His baptism, the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness, where He was tempted for forty days.

jerusalem.name: Jerusalem
jerusalem.desc: Jesus rode into the city on a colt, cleansed the temple, and debated and taught in its courts; the Last Supper, the trial before the Sanhedrin, and Pilate's sentence all took place here.

gerasa.name: Gerasa
gerasa.desc: On the east shore of the Sea of Galilee, in the region of the Gerasenes, Jesus drove the unclean spirits out of a man who lived among the tombs, and they entered the pigs.

bethsaida.name: Bethsaida
bethsaida.desc: Jesus sent His disciples ahead by boat to Bethsaida; later, here, He laid His hands on a blind man twice, and the man saw clearly.

tyre.name: Tyre
tyre.desc: In the region of Tyre, a Syrophoenician woman fell at Jesus' feet and begged Him to drive the demon out of her daughter.

caesarea.name: Caesarea Philippi
caesarea.desc: On the way to the villages of Caesarea Philippi, Peter declared that Jesus is the Christ, and Jesus first spoke plainly of the suffering ahead of Him.

jericho.name: Jericho
jericho.desc: As Jesus was leaving Jericho, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar sitting by the road, cried out to Him and at once received his sight.

bethany.name: Bethany
bethany.desc: During His last days in Jerusalem, Jesus stayed at Bethany; in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman poured perfume on His head.

olives.name: Mount of Olives
olives.desc: Sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Jesus spoke of the last things; after the supper He came here again and foretold that Peter would deny Him.

gethsemane.name: Gethsemane
gethsemane.desc: Here Jesus fell to the ground and prayed while the disciples slept; Judas came with a crowd and gave a kiss as the signal to arrest Him.

golgotha.name: Golgotha
golgotha.desc: The name means “The Place of the Skull.” Here Jesus was crucified and breathed His last; very early on the first day of the week, the tomb where He had been laid was empty.

bethlehem.name: Bethlehem
bethlehem.desc: Bethlehem in Judea, where Jesus was born. The Magi followed the star here; on coming to the house, they saw the Child with His mother Mary, and they fell down and worshiped Him.

nain.name: Nain
nain.desc: As Jesus approached the town gate, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother, a widow. He touched the coffin and said, “Young man, I tell you, get up!” And the dead man sat up and began to speak.

emmaus.name: Emmaus
emmaus.desc: A village about seven miles from Jerusalem. On the day of the resurrection, Jesus Himself walked along with two disciples; at the table He broke the bread, their eyes were opened, and they recognized Him.

cana.name: Cana
cana.desc: Cana in Galilee. At a wedding here Jesus turned the water into wine, the first of His signs; later, from here, with a word He healed the royal official's son who lay sick at Capernaum.

sychar.name: Sychar
sychar.desc: A town in Samaria near the plot of ground Jacob had given to his son Joseph; Jacob's well was there. Weary from His journey, Jesus sat down by the well and asked a Samaritan woman who came to draw water for a drink.

创造时期.name: Creation
创造时期.desc: God creates the heavens and the earth, and makes mankind.

出埃及时期.name: The Exodus
出埃及时期.desc: God leads Israel out of Egypt.

士师时期.name: The Judges
士师时期.desc: God raises up judges to rescue His people.

被掳与归回.name: Exile and Return
被掳与归回.desc: Carried off to Babylon, then home again to rebuild.
